text: Pogacar's relentless aggression has left rivals scrambling tactically, but Stage 13's brutal finish—the historic Ballon d'Alsace arriving after 2400m of climbing—is tailor-made to expose any accumulated fatigue. Vingegaard, already bleeding time to both Evenepoel and Ayuso, cannot afford another defensive day; his team needs to either force the pace early on the Col des Croix or gamble on a late attack before the final climb sorts the wheat from chaff. Evenepoel's recent gains suggest Red Bull-Bora has found a rhythm Visma can't match, which means Pogacar may finally face real pressure to control rather than attack—a subtle but crucial shift in who dictates the race's tempo.
